summary: Intermittent SSO failures for contractor accounts via Okta AD Bridge (SAML assertion time skew)
description:
Issue summary: Several contractor users report intermittent failures when signing in to Redwood internal apps using Okta SSO that is routed through our on-prem Active Directory via the Okta AD Bridge. Failures manifest as immediate SAML assertion rejections or 'Invalid assertion' errors.

Impact: ~8 contractors (~5% of current contractors) cannot authenticate reliably to the console and CI dashboards. Business impact: delays for contractors completing sprint tasks; a few hourly CI jobs that use contractor service accounts failed to start. Incident started 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC and recurred sporadically.

Environment: Production; affected region us-east. Affected account types: contractor user accounts provisioned via SCIM with on-prem AD backed group mapping to Okta groups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Attempt to sign in to console using Okta SSO (SAML) from an affected contractor account
2) Observe either successful login or an immediate SAML error screen saying 'Invalid SAML assertion' or 'Assertion invalid: NotBefore condition failed'
3) Retry after ~30-90 seconds; login may succeed intermittently
4) Reproduction more common from contractor office network (on-prem) than home networks
logs: Okta SAML logs (example): Assertion rejected: conditions failed: NotBefore=2026-03-10T08:22:31Z, Now=2026-03-10T08:21:59Z
AD Bridge agent logs: skews_detected=true, ntp_sync_status=unsynced on host ad-bridge-03
Proxy TLS logs: no related TLS handshake failures observed
Console auth service logs: 401 from Okta for user u/contractor-janed; SAML error code 0x42
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SAML assertion clock skew leading to NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter validation failures. Okta accepts assertions only if assertion validity window lines up with Okta's clock tolerance.
AD Bridge host ad-bridge-03 shows NTP drift (~45s) vs other bridge hosts (<=3s). Drift aligns with observed NotBefore offsets in Okta logs.
Issue highly correlated with contractor accounts provisioned to on-prem AD groups (SCIM mapping path). Internal staff sign-ins using cloud-only Okta paths not affected.
Repro across multiple contractor IPs suggests source is assertion generation (AD Bridge) rather than customer network.
Related historical ticket INT-20671 noted role propagation delays but not clock skew; linking for audit trail and because both affect contractor RBAC mappings.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:05 - Aisha Kapoor: Investigating. Pulled Okta SAML debug logs for affected users and matched NotBefore timestamps to AD Bridge host times.
2026-03-10 09:27 - DevOps (R. Kim): ad-bridge-03 NTP service reported 'unsynchronized'. Restarted ntpd; awaiting monitoring to confirm re-sync.
2026-03-10 09:40 - Aisha Kapoor: After NTP restart, two previously failing contractor logins succeeded. Marking as potential mitigation; monitoring for recurrence.
2026-03-10 11:12 - Security (M. Alvarez): Confirmed no evidence of replay or tampering. This appears operational (clock skew) rather than security incident.

2026-03-11 07:55 - SRE (J. Li): Implemented configuration change to increase Okta assertion tolerance window for AD Bridge SAML responses by +60s as emergency mitigation while we roll out permanent fix.

2026-03-12 10:03 - Aisha Kapoor: Root cause identified: intermittent NTP daemon crash on ad-bridge-03 after recent package upgrade. Patch prepared. Scheduling maintenance to roll patch to other bridges.
2026-03-12 14:20 - Aisha Kapoor: Patch rolled to ad-bridge-01..04, NTP drift eliminated; no new SAML assertion errors observed in 24h. Planning follow-up runbook updates.
resolution: Mitigation: Restarted NTP and increased Okta tolerance window early to reduce immediate failures. Root cause: NTP daemon crash (post-package upgrade) on ad-bridge-03 causing clock skew and SAML assertion NotBefore mismatches. Fix: patched NTP package and deployed to all AD Bridge hosts; added healthcheck alert for NTP drift >10s. Follow-ups: update AD Bridge upgrade playbook to include post-upgrade NTP validation, add unit tests for assertion timestamp generation, and schedule a postmortem runbook entry. Incident status: monitoring; no new occurrences after patch as of 2026-03-12.
